description: pyBIMstab is a Python model for checking the factor of safety against sliding in two-dimensional slopes. Its project publishes a limit-equilibrium calculation for homogeneous slopes and block-in-matrix materials. Users enter slope coordinates, soil or rock strength, block distribution and a water table. The software constructs circular or tortuous candidate slip surfaces, with an A-star search for tortuous paths, and calculates safety factors with the General Limit Equilibrium method. Coverage is one user-defined slope cross-section; spatial resolution follows its geometry and block tiling, and there is no fixed time period. The public GitHub source, examples and documentation are available under BSD-2-Clause at no code cost. These outputs could support landslide screening for a road cutting, rail corridor or built site before a broader disruption simulation. A limitation is that a two-dimensional limit-equilibrium result cannot represent all three-dimensional geology or determine network-level service loss. No related catalogue record was identified. Python dependencies are listed, but no field case or code execution was verified.
